Website Maintenance · Dallas, TX

Website Maintenance in Dallas, TX: Keep Your Business Site Secure, Fast and Up — and Be the Business Customers Find When They Search or Ask AI

This page is for Dallas business owners whose website is their front door — law offices, clinics, contractors, agencies, restaurants and e-commerce stores — and who cannot afford it to be down, slow, hacked or quietly broken when a customer searches Google Maps or asks ChatGPT for a recommendation. Dallas is one of the most competitive business markets in the country; a site that is down for an afternoon or slow on a phone hands the customer to the next result on Preston Road. We take over the security, updates, backups, speed and monthly changes for a flat monthly fee, repair what is already broken first, and report every month in plain language. The next step is a free live error check of your site.

  • Texas-based since 2013; 1,000+ websites repaired, 500+ designed
  • Fixes in 2–4 hours, 24/7 support, no upfront payment
  • Maintenance from $300/month, month-to-month, cancel with 7 days’ notice
Get a Free Live Error Check
Call 832-266-7209

What the work is aimed at

  1. BaselineUptime, load time, plugin inventory, open vulnerabilities, backup status and whether forms actually deliver.
  2. Repair and hardenFix what is broken now; firewall, login protection, least-privilege users, unused plugins removed.
  3. RhythmStaged updates with rollback, tested backups, monitoring that alerts a human.
  4. Measured outcomeUptime, speed, vulnerabilities closed, backups verified and changes made — reported monthly.
On this page
  1. AI search & GEO
  2. Summary
  3. Why sites break
  4. Security evidence
  5. How customers find you
  6. What we improve
  7. How we work
  8. Dallas businesses we maintain

  10. Scope and cost
  11. Questions

AI search, GEO and AEO

How AI search changes what a Dallas business website has to do — and why maintenance now affects GEO and AEO

Customers no longer work through ten blue links. They act on the first AI summary, the first spoken answer or the first three map pins. AI engines only cite sites they can read, trust and reach: a site that is down, slow, throwing errors or serving injected spam is not just losing visitors, it is being skipped by the machines that now answer the question. The four searches below show where that decision is made.

  • Google Maps“[your service] near me”Answered by the local pack; a broken website link or a profile pointing to an error page quietly drops you.
  • ChatGPT / Gemini“Who is a reliable [your service] in Dallas?”The assistant names two or three businesses whose public data is consistent and whose pages it could fetch and understand.
  • Google AI Mode“How much does [your service] cost in Dallas?”AI answers cite the clearest source; a page that loads slowly or is blocked by a security misconfiguration is not that source.
  • Voice“Hey Google, is [your business] open now?”One spoken answer from your business profile and website facts; stale or conflicting data gives a wrong answer or none.

How it influences the choice

A 2026 study that ran 24,000 real queries through Google across 243 countries found AI-generated answers on 65% of general-knowledge queries and 58% of health queries in 2025, with AI answering steadily more commercial and shopping queries each year. Source: The Rise of AI Search (arXiv, 2026). Separately, BrightEdge, Dec 2025 found Google keeps AI answers off “near me” local searches, so Maps and reviews still decide the local choice. Either way the engine needs a working, readable, consistent site to choose you — which is what maintenance protects.

Why GEO and AEO are important

GEO (generative engine optimisation) is being the source an AI engine cites: consistent business facts everywhere, structured data, pages that answer directly, reviews that are recent and answered. AEO (answer engine optimisation) is writing each page so the first paragraph is the answer. Both depend on a site that is up, fast, secure and crawlable — the unglamorous things maintenance does every month. We keep the technical floor solid as part of the plan, and quote GEO/AEO content work separately when you want it.

No agency can guarantee an AI citation or a Maps position; what maintenance controls is that your site is never the reason you were skipped.

The short version

What website maintenance in Dallas does, and what it cannot promise

What it does: keeps your WordPress or business website secure, updated, backed up, fast and online, and handles the content, form and integration changes you need each month — so the site keeps doing its job of turning a search into a call or a booking.

Who it helps: Dallas–Fort Worth businesses with a WordPress or business website that generates leads or sales: professional services, medical and dental practices, contractors, agencies, hospitality and online stores — single sites or portfolios of client sites.

What changes: no more white screens after an update, no more “the form stopped sending,” no more discovering a hack from a customer’s email, and a monthly report you can read in five minutes.

What it cannot guarantee: that no attacker will ever get in, that your host will never go down, or that a third-party service will never change. What we guarantee is the response: 24/7 support, 2–4 hour fixes, and you pay after the work is done.

The problem

Why a Dallas business website breaks, and why nobody notices until it costs a customer

Dallas businesses tend to have sites built fast by an agency that has since moved on, then extended by two or three freelancers. The result is exactly what breaks:

Plugins nobody owns

The site runs thirty plugins installed by three different freelancers; several are abandoned, and 91% of WordPress vulnerabilities are in plugins.

Updates that break the site

An update goes live without testing, the page builder conflicts with the theme, and the homepage is blank until someone notices.

Backups that have never been restored

The host says there are backups. Nobody has ever tested one. The day it matters is the day it fails.

Forms that stopped sending

A mail setting changed months ago; leads have been going nowhere since, and the business thinks the phone just got quieter.

Slow pages on an old PHP version

Six-second loads on mobile, an unsupported PHP version, and no caching — customers leave and rankings slide.

A hack discovered by a customer

Redirects to a casino site, spam pages in Google, a security warning in the browser — found by a customer, not the owner.

Market evidence

Why maintenance is a security job first: what happened to WordPress in 2025

Metric: new security vulnerabilities disclosed in the WordPress ecosystem (core, plugins, themes) per year, with year-over-year change. Scope: global. Data period: calendar years 2022–2025. Source: Patchstack, State of WordPress Security in 2026 (data updated 25 Feb 2026). Method: counts as published from the Patchstack vulnerability database. Limitation: vendor-maintained database; disclosure counts measure what was found and reported, not what was exploited on any given site.
YearVulnerabilities disclosedChange
20224,528—
20235,948+31%
20247,966+34%
202511,334+42%
  • 91% of the 2025 vulnerabilities were in plugins and 9% in themes; WordPress core itself had six, all low risk. 46% had no developer patch available at the moment of disclosure, and the weighted median time from disclosure to first mass exploitation was five hours. Source: Patchstack, State of WordPress Security in 2026. Implication: “keep WordPress updated” is necessary but not sufficient — a maintained site needs a firewall, monitoring, plugin pruning and someone watching the disclosures, because nearly half of the holes cannot be patched by clicking Update.

How discovery works

Two funnels: how a customer reaches your site, and how a business finds us

The customer’s path (your funnel)

  • A need arises and the customer searches on a phone — Maps, Google, or an AI assistant.
  • Your listing or an AI answer sends them to the website.
  • The site has to load fast, be secure, show the right hours and prices, and let them call or submit a form.
  • The form has to deliver, and the call has to connect.
  • Any break in that chain — down, slow, hacked, form dead — is a customer who never existed as far as you know.

The owner’s path (our funnel, so you know how we think)

  • An owner or office manager has a broken site, a scary security email, or a freelancer who stopped answering.
  • They search “website maintenance Dallas” or ask an assistant who fixes WordPress sites.
  • They read this page, see real prices and a real Texas business, and want the problem looked at rather than a pitch.
  • They request a live error check; we share a screen and show the actual problems.
  • We measure our own work by qualified consultations, exactly as we measure your site’s uptime and leads.

This page is written for business owners and office managers. We maintain and repair websites; we are not your hosting company, and we will tell you plainly when the host is the problem.

What we improve

Six things a Dallas maintenance plan actually changes

Security hardening and monitoring

Deliverables: web application firewall, login protection, file-change and uptime monitoring, malware scanning, vulnerability watch on every installed component.

Why: 91% of WordPress vulnerabilities are in plugins and nearly half ship unpatched; monitoring is what closes that gap.

Limit: no system is unhackable; we reduce exposure and respond fast, we do not promise immunity.

Staged updates with rollback

Deliverables: core, plugin and theme updates tested on a copy first, applied on a schedule, rolled back automatically if anything breaks.

Why: most “the site went white” calls are an untested update.

Backups that are actually restorable

Deliverables: daily off-site backups with retention, and a monthly test restore so the backup is proven, not assumed.

Why: an untested backup is a hope, not a plan.

Speed and hosting health

Deliverables: caching, image optimisation, database clean-up, PHP on a supported version, hosting review and migration when the host is the problem.

Why: slow sites lose customers and rank lower.

Content, form and integration changes

Deliverables: your text, image, page and menu edits; form routing and notification fixes; CRM, booking and payment integrations kept working.

Why: a maintained site is one you can actually change without fear.

Limit: large new builds or redesigns are quoted separately.

Reporting and change log

Deliverables: a monthly plain-language report of uptime, speed, vulnerabilities closed, backups verified, changes made and incidents, with response times.

Why: you should be able to see what you paid for.

How we work toward the goal

The maintenance flow, with the decisions built in

  1. Establish the goal and baselineAgree what “maintained” means for you (uptime, speed, security, content changes) and record current uptime, load time, plugin inventory and open vulnerabilities.
  2. Audit and inventoryEvery plugin, theme, user, integration, form and cron job; hosting, PHP version, backups and DNS.
  3. Repair what is broken nowErrors, conflicts, broken forms, slow pages, malware or redirects — fixed first, usually within 2–4 hours.
  4. Harden and reduceFirewall, login protection, least-privilege users, unused plugins removed, PHP on a supported version.
  5. Set the update and backup rhythmStaged updates with rollback, off-site backups tested by restoring them, uptime and change monitoring.
  6. Keep search and AI visibility intactRedirects, sitemaps, structured data and page speed checked after every change so maintenance never costs rankings or citations.
  7. Content and form changesYour monthly edits, new pages and form routing handled inside the plan, with a change log.
  8. MeasureMonthly report: uptime, speed, vulnerabilities closed, backups verified, changes made, incidents and response times.
  9. RefineAdjust the plan to what the report shows — more hardening, fewer plugins, a faster host.
  10. Feedback loopSteps 8 and 9 repeat monthly; steps 3–6 reopen whenever monitoring or a disclosure points back at them.

Decision points

  • If the site is already compromisedClean, restore from a verified backup, rotate every credential and close the entry point before any routine work.
  • If an update breaks somethingRoll back from staging, isolate the conflicting plugin, report it, and re-apply when a fix exists.
  • If a disclosed vulnerability has no patchVirtual-patch at the firewall, disable or replace the component, and watch for exploitation — 46% of 2025 disclosures arrived without a fix.
  • Optional branch: redesign or SEOQuoted separately and only when the maintained site is stable; never bundled into a maintenance fee.

Dallas businesses

The kinds of Dallas businesses we maintain sites for, and what each one needs

Maintenance looks different for a Uptown law firm, a Plano dental group and a Deep Ellum restaurant. These are the Dallas business types we maintain most and what each plan emphasises.

  • LAWLaw offices and professional servicesLead forms, intake routing and reputation; downtime is lost cases.
  • MEDMedical and dental practicesBooking integrations, HIPAA-conscious forms, review flow; see our healthcare pages for marketing.
  • TRADEContractors and home servicesCall tracking, quote forms, seasonal landing pages, fast mobile pages.
  • AGENCYAgencies and consultantsWhite-label maintenance for client portfolios with a single report per client.
  • HOSPRestaurants and hospitalityMenus, reservations, hours accuracy across Google and the site.
  • SHOPE-commerceWooCommerce updates tested before go-live, payment and inventory integrations watched.

How we scope a plan: by what the site does for the business (lead capture, booking, e-commerce, information), how many plugins and integrations it depends on, how often content changes, and how costly an hour of downtime is. We do not claim an office in Dallas; we are Houston-based and maintain sites across Texas and all 50 states remotely, with 24/7 support.

Content and website architecture

What a maintainable business website looks like

1

Core and theme

A supported theme, a supported PHP version, and WordPress core current; nothing custom-hacked into core files.

2

Plugins

Only what the site uses, each actively maintained, each with a known owner; abandoned plugins replaced.

3

Backups, staging, logs

Off-site backups, a staging copy for updates, and an activity log so every change has a who and a when.

4

Monitoring and alerts

Uptime, file changes, vulnerability disclosures and form deliverability watched; alerts go to a human who acts.

A maintainable site has fewer moving parts, each one owned and monitored. The first month of a plan usually removes more than it adds.

Scope, timing and investment

What is included, what it depends on, and what moves the cost

Included in a maintenance plan

  • Security hardening, firewall and monitoring
  • Staged updates with rollback
  • Daily off-site backups with monthly test restore
  • Speed, PHP and hosting health checks
  • Monthly content, form and integration changes
  • Monthly plain-language report and change log

Dependencies and timing

Repairs are usually done within 2–4 hours. The first month covers inventory, hardening and the update/backup rhythm; from the second month the plan runs on schedule. Hosting migrations, when the host is the problem, are scheduled around your quiet hours. Response times are stated in every monthly report.

What affects cost

Number of sites, how many plugins and integrations they run, whether the site is already damaged, and how fast you need a response. Website maintenance starts at $300 per month per site; one-off website fixes start at $50; hacked-website repair is $200. There is no upfront payment — you pay after the fix is done — and ongoing plans are month-to-month, cancellable with 7 days’ notice. Design, SEO, GEO and Google Ads are quoted separately so you always know which dollar did what.

Proof and expertise

What you can verify about us before a call

Since 2013

Fix Website Issues is a DBA of Bizzsol LLC, a Texas-registered business based in Houston, serving all 50 states.

1,000+ websites repaired

Repair is our origin and still our most common job; 2–4 hours is the typical fix time and support is 24/7.

500+ websites designed or redesigned

Counted separately from repairs, across WordPress and headless WordPress.

Pay after the fix

$0 upfront. We show you the live errors first, fix them, and you pay when it works.

We publish client results only with the client’s permission, a stated timeframe, a baseline and the measurement method. Where that permission has not been given, we show our process instead of inventing numbers.

Questions Dallas business owners ask

Website maintenance in Dallas: direct answers

Do you need to be in Dallas to maintain our site?

No. Maintenance is remote work by nature — monitoring, updates, backups and fixes happen on the server, not in your office. We are a Houston-based Texas business, we work in your time zone, and support is 24/7. For anything that needs a physical presence (hosting hardware, in-office network), we tell you plainly it is outside what a website maintenance plan covers.

What is included in $300 a month?

Security hardening and monitoring, staged core/plugin/theme updates with rollback, daily off-site backups with a monthly test restore, speed and hosting checks, reasonable monthly content and form changes, and a plain-language report. Larger projects (redesigns, new sections, SEO campaigns) are quoted separately so the maintenance fee stays predictable.

Our site is already hacked — is that maintenance?

No, that is a repair, and it comes first. Hacked-website repair is $200: we clean the site, restore from a verified backup, rotate credentials and close the entry point. Maintenance starts after the site is clean, so you are not paying monthly for a site that is still compromised.

Can’t we just turn on auto-updates?

Auto-updates help, but in 2025 46% of disclosed WordPress vulnerabilities had no patch when they were made public, and the median time to mass exploitation was five hours. Updates also break things. Maintenance means someone tests the update, applies it, watches the disclosures for the components you run, and virtual-patches what cannot be updated.

How fast do you respond when something breaks?

Support is 24/7 and most fixes take 2–4 hours. A monitored site usually tells us before you notice. We state response times in the monthly report so you can hold us to them.

Do you maintain sites you didn’t build?

Yes — most of the sites we maintain were built by someone else. We start with the inventory and repair step, and we will tell you plainly if a site is better rebuilt than maintained.

What can you control, and what can’t you?

We control how quickly vulnerabilities are closed, whether backups restore, whether updates are tested, and how fast we respond. We do not control your hosting company’s outages, third-party services going down, or attackers finding a brand-new zero-day; what we control is how quickly and cleanly the site recovers.

Do you only maintain WordPress?

WordPress and headless WordPress are most of what we do, and most Dallas business sites run on it. We also repair and maintain other common platforms; we will tell you during the live check if a site is outside what we can support well.

Start with a free live error check

A screen-shared session where we check your site’s errors, speed, security, backups, forms and plugins and show you exactly what we found. No upfront charge, no obligation, and if we fix something you pay after it works.

What to have ready

  • Your website address and who hosts it
  • Any error, warning or symptom you have seen
  • Any current freelancer, agency or maintenance plan

What happens next: we run the live check, send a short written list of findings, and quote repairs and the monthly plan separately. Plans are month-to-month with no upfront payment; cancel with 7 days’ notice.
